theme.styleDescription: Choose the color theme and interface shape separately. Any combination can be used, and changes apply immediately and save automatically.

soft.name: Soft
soft.description: Keeps the current CC-Panes corner treatment and light borders, so the upgrade does not change the existing appearance.

slab.name: Slab
slab.description: Uses tighter corners and subtle top-and-bottom edge contrast to distinguish adjacent panels.

sharp.name: Sharp
sharp.description: Removes container rounding so tabs, sidebars, and panels align to the grid.

glass.name: Glass
glass.description: Uses translucent, blurred chrome for the title bar, sidebar, and overlays while keeping terminals and inputs solid.

panel.name: Panel
panel.description: Uses square corners and clearer dividers to define panes and tool regions.

carbon.name: Carbon
carbon.description: Adds a low-contrast geometric texture to translucent surfaces while keeping terminal content clear.

webAccessDescription: Start the local Web app with the same CC-Panes data. LAN access requires account credentials.

webAccessSection.autoOpen: Open the browser automatically after startup
webAccessSection.autoOpenHint: Useful when using the Web app as the default entry point.

webAccessSection.remoteAuthenticatedWrite: Allow authenticated remote sessions to write

Confirm that the remote link is trusted (Tailscale is recommended). Restart the Web service after saving.
webAccessSection.remoteAuthenticatedWriteRequiresAuthHint: Enable account login and set a password first; this switch has no effect without a configured password.
webAccessSection.ipWhitelistHint: Leave blank to allow any LAN client; separate multiple entries with newlines or commas.

orchestrator.title: MCP orchestrator listener
orchestrator.description: Built-in CC-Panes orchestrator (for CLI ccpanes MCP tools to connect back). Restart the app after changing.

auto.label: Automatic (recommended)
auto.hint: Defaults to local-only; WSL can access loopback on mirrored networking, while NAT-mode WSL opens all network interfaces.

loopback.label: Local only
loopback.hint: Always 127.0.0.1. WSL can still access it on mirrored networking; in NAT mode, the CLI inside WSL may not be able to connect back to MCP.

all.label: All interfaces
all.hint: Always 0.0.0.0 (visible on the LAN, protected by a random port and token).

tailscale.title: Tailscale remote access (recommended)
tailscale.description: Securely access the Web app from your own devices through Tailscale Serve: no LAN exposure is needed and the service stays bound to localhost. CC-Panes only performs read-only detection; it does not execute commands or store Tailscale credentials.
tailscale.cliNotFound: Tailscale CLI not detected. Install it and try again: https://tailscale.com/download

tailscale.tailnetHint: Run the command above in a terminal, then access this address from any device in your tailnet. We recommend enabling "Account password login" and "Remote read-only mode"; Tailscale access is treated as a remote source. To unpublish, run

webAccessSection.restartHint: Changes to the port, LAN access, or password policy take effect after restarting the Web service.

ccchanPetDescriptionDoro: A tiny white chibi pet with pink hair, purple eyes, and a side rose ribbon. Codex-pet standard atlas.
ccchanPetDescriptionYeShunguang: A school-themed companion inspired by Ye Shunguang from Zenless Zone Zero, carrying a notebook and pencil to accompany you while you work, wait, review, and sprint.
ccchanWanderHint: When off, cc-chan stays put and never moves on its own; you can still drag it.
ccchanSkinDirHint: Create <pet-id>/pet.json plus a spritesheet in this directory to add a custom pet; a pet with the same id as a built-in one overrides its appearance.
rendererHint: Auto uses the DOM renderer on Windows (WebGL has known CJK glyph-atlas corruption) and prefers WebGL on other Chromium hosts; choosing WebGL explicitly still enables it.
pathLinksEnabledHint: Show file and directory paths in terminal output as clickable links with open actions.
showContextUsageHint: Show the context usage indicator in the global and per-terminal status bars.
showStatusBarHint: The per-terminal status bar (CLI label, model, context usage, project path) only appears in multi-pane layouts; with a single or fullscreen pane the same information lives in the global status bar. When off it is not rendered at all, giving the space back to the terminal. Toggle quickly via right-click on any status bar.

voiceShowFloatingButtonDesc: Hides the microphone button in the terminal corner; the voice shortcut still works.
voiceEnableItn: Enable ITN for numbers, dates, and formatting
voiceLimitHint: This uses the Qwen-ASR OpenAI-compatible sync API for short recordings; the backend rejects audio over 10 MB.
voiceMimoHint: Xiaomi MiMo uses the open-platform audio understanding API. CC-Panes converts recordings to WAV locally and sends Base64 audio; use mimo-v2.5 or mimo-v2-omni.
shortcutsHint: Click a shortcut then press a new key combination to change it, press Esc to cancel
socksWarning: SOCKS5 proxy may not be supported by all tools (e.g. Claude Code, npm). HTTP proxy is recommended, or use a local proxy client to convert SOCKS5 to HTTP.

interfaceShapes.title: Try interface shapes
interfaceShapes.body: Keep your current colors and change only the corners, dividers, and surface treatment.

dispatchOrchestration.title: Let one AI command a fleet of AIs
dispatchOrchestration.body: Say "run these in parallel" and this session splits the work, spawns several Claude / Codex workers, and each one reports back on its own when it finishes. You only start it and wrap it up. The orchestration panel shows every worker's live status.

worktreeIsolation.title: Work in parallel without touching your main tree
worktreeIsolation.body: A worktree checks out another branch into its own directory, so each dispatched worker edits its own copy while your main working tree stays clean. Right-click a project → "Worktree Manager" to create, remove, or open a terminal inside one.

aiPanel.title: Let the AI render a real panel for you
aiPanel.body: An AI in a terminal can only emit characters. Over MCP it can post a Markdown or HTML panel instead: comparison tables, progress boards, even buttons for you to decide with. Panels land in the right dock, and closing one keeps its content in history.

skills.title: Common workflows are already baked into the AI
skills.body: Parallel dispatch, plan handoff, peer review, wrap-up checks — these are shipped as skills and installed into each CLI by CC-Panes. Plain language triggers them; for the full list type `/` in a session (Codex uses the `ccpanes-` prefix), or open Resource Hub → Skills and read the "built-in CC-Panes skills" section.

rightDock.title: The right dock: watch while it runs
rightDock.body: The panel button in the title bar, just left of the gear, opens the right dock: which files the AI touched, Git changes, AI panels, and session history all live there, and it can stay open alongside the left sidebar. It has no shortcut, and it starts collapsed on every launch.

browserTab.title: The browser is the AI's hand, not yours
browserTab.body: A real browser can run in a split pane, but there is no "new browser tab" button — the AI opens it over MCP: let it load your dev server, take a screenshot, click around, and run a snippet of JS to verify a change instead of just claiming it works. Screenshots, clicks, and JS evaluation are Windows-only today.

systemEnvNone: No Anthropic environment variables or cc-switch config detected
systemEnvRuntimeWarning: This probe inspects the local host process; it does not represent the target environment under {{runtime}}.
resumeIdBackfillHint: Legacy mechanism that guesses resume ids by scanning session directories. Superseded by deterministic binding (Claude issued id / Codex title capture). Keep off unless troubleshooting.
lowerSessionPriorityHint: Runs each session's process tree (the CLI and everything it spawns — cargo, rg, npm) at below-normal priority so a busy pane can't starve the UI. Idle cores are still used fully, so build throughput is unaffected. Applies to newly started sessions.
terminalDaemonHint: Host PTYs in a standalone daemon so desktop, Web and mobile attach to the same live sessions. Takes effect after app restart.
daemonOrphanTtlHint: Idle sessions with no viewer and no recent output are reclaimed oldest-first after this duration (default 24 hours). Applies within ~1 minute, no restart needed.
daemonOrphanReaperDisabledHint: When checked the daemon never auto-reclaims unwatched sessions (replaces the old "set expiry to 0" semantics).
orphanSessionReclaimedBody: Cleaned up {{count}} background terminal sessions with no panel reference.
disableWslUsageScanDesc: Stop scanning usage data inside WSL so the app never wakes the WSL VM (Vmmem memory usage)
showSystemResources: Show system resources in the status bar
allowMcpYoloProfiles: Allow agents to manage YOLO launch profiles
allowMcpYoloProfilesHint: Allow orchestration agents to create, bind, or explicitly launch profiles with --dangerously-skip-permissions. Agents can bypass permission prompts when enabled; turn this on only if you accept that risk.
followAgentLaunch: Follow agent launches to their layout
followAgentLaunchHint: When off (default), workers a leader launches are still created in the target layout, but the view stays where you are — a toast with a jump link is shown instead. Turn on to restore automatic switching.
